methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops targeting Hampton Roads residents signal grassroots capability building outside traditional tech hubs, directly addressing the technology gap through distributed peer education rather than platform dependence.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU's institutional partnership with AI Ready RVA concentrates deep AI education and innovation infrastructure in the state capital, potentially creating a secondary hub but not yet indicating rural knowledge distribution mechanisms.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches WorkAI Lab to prepare leaders for new era of technology - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's WorkAI Lab represents intentional deep capability building in a non-metro region, suggesting peer network development that could challenge the concentration pattern if sustained beyond initial launch.

signals.title: TAYLOR: AI data centers increase Virginia’s urban-rural divide - The Cavalier Daily
signals.signal_reading: Commentary explicitly naming the urban-rural divide around AI data centers reveals infrastructure benefits concentrating in NoVA while other regions lack both the economic gains and skill development pathways.

signals.title: Norfolk businesses are being urged not to miss out on the benefits of artificial intelligence - Rayo
signals.signal_reading: Urging Norfolk businesses to adopt AI without emphasis on deep skill development suggests platform-layer consumption rather than foundational capability building, risking shallow distributed adoption dependent on vendor tools.
